chief_complaint: cola-colored urine and swelling around my eyes
hpi_details: 22F presents with 2 days of dark, 'cola-colored' urine and swelling around her eyes in the morning. She had a severe sore throat 2 weeks ago that was not treated with antibiotics.

core_concepts: Nephritic syndrome presentation: hematuria, hypertension, edema, and mild-to-moderate proteinuria.
Typically occurs 1-3 weeks after Strep pharyngitis or 3-6 weeks after skin infection.
common_misconceptions: Assuming all red/brown urine is simply a UTI or stone (must look for dysmorphic RBCs or casts).
dangerous_errors: Missing the hypertension that accompanies acute nephritic syndrome.
management_principles: Supportive care, treat hypertension and edema, check ASO titer, low C3 levels.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 22F with recent untreated pharyngitis presents with gross hematuria and periorbital edema.
reference_soap.objective: BP 160/95. Periorbital edema present. Urinalysis: large blood, 1+ protein, RBC casts.
reference_soap.plan: Check ASO titer, C3/C4 complement, BMP. Treat BP with diuretics/calcium channel blockers if needed. Nephrology consult.

learning_objectives: Identify the classic features of acute nephritic syndrome.

teaching.one_liner: Cola-colored urine, periorbital edema, and hypertension following a recent sore throat, classic for nephritic syndrome.

must_ask.say: When did you first notice your urine looking cola-colored or brown?
Did you have a sore throat or a skin infection in the past few weeks?
Where have you noticed swelling, especially around your eyes in the morning?
Have you had any headaches or blurry vision that could be related to high blood pressure?
Has the amount of urine you're passing changed recently?
